subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Has"** is the **correct form of the verb **to use here, aligning with the** present perfect tense of the sentence structure.**
 
• The** present perfect tense ("has broken") **indicates an action that occurred at an unspecified time before now.
 
• In this context, **the present perfect tense is used to describe an action (breaking the door) that has a present relevance (the valuables are stolen).**
 
• Using **"has" **ensures **subject-verb agreement, as "somebody" is singular and requires a singular verb form.**
 
• **"Has broken"** is a commonly used, grammatically** correct **phrase that fits well in conversational and narrative contexts.
 
• Maintaining the correct verb tense is crucial for the coherence and** readability of the passage.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (have):** **"Have"** is a plural verb form, unsuitable for the singular subject** "somebody."**
 
• **Option 3 (shall have):** **"Shall have"** is future perfect tense, inappropriate for the context of the story.
 
• **Option 4 (had):** **"Had"** is past perfect tense, which is not suitable here since the action is relevant to the present.
